newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold steady with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold steady with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady Friday in fairly sluggish trade, underpinned by a stable crude market and some utility fuel switching interest from more expensive natural gas.

"Fuel is definitely cheaper than gas, but it all depends on weather. If the East heats up, you should see the low sulphur move up," said one cash trader, noting fuel oil stocks were in good shape amid little or no demand.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly today to $15.00-25 a barrel after a sharp crude rally on Thursday drove prices up, traders said.
Forecasts for more moderate eastern temperatures next week offered little hope for better utility demand near-term despite resid's competitive edge to gas, traders said.
Early one percent paper quotes showed little change, with NYH May still in the $15.50-70 range and June at $16 or better, but some said values may have slipped slightly later in the day.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour again notionally held steady at about $16, traders said.
New York high sulphurs also were flat from Thursday, with 2.2 percent still pegged at about $14.50.
At the U.S. Gulf, three percent remained talked at about $14, while one percent also held steady at $14.75.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate weekend gas prices eased several cents Friday to the mid-$2.50s/mmBtu, or about $16.07 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, slipped a nickel to about $2.30/mmBtu, or $14.49 a barrel.
